newsitem.title: USA: US energy secretary should not be grounded - Curtis.
newsitem.headline: US energy secretary should not be grounded - Curtis.

text.p: Acting U.S. Energy Secretary Charles Curtis Tuesday urged Congress not to ground the next energy secretary in the wake of complaints that former Secretary Hazel O'Leary traveled excessively.
"I think it would be a mistake to keep the secretary of energy home," Curtis told the House Commerce Energy and Power subcommittee.
Federico Pena is slated to become the next energy secretary, with the Senate Energy Committee expected to approve his nomination Wednesday.
Curtis, who was assistant secretary to O'Leary, has said only that he would stay at the department until Pena is confirmed.
Curtis told the committee that the energy secretary must travel to meet with counterparts in countries such as Russia, Caspian Sea nations and other nations that are major potential oil suppliers.

"That represents the meaningful capacity to diversify world oil supply. Those are all governmentally controlled markets. The ability to influence that development requires cabinet, ministerial level interaction," he said.

"Similarly, what happens in China, India, Pakistan -- the energy choices that those countries make will determine not only the world's oil balance but environmental quality in very significant respects," he said.

O'Leary came under fire last year from the Republican-led Congress for her extensive international travels, often with large business-sector entourages, to spur export business for U.S. energy companies.
